name: env
summary: Prints the environment, or runs a command with a modified environment.
description: Without an argument, env lists every environment variable. Followed by assignments and a command, it runs that command with the given variables, without changing the current shell. You also see it on the first line of scripts: #!/usr/bin/env python3 finds python3 in the PATH, wherever it is installed.

options.description: Removes a variable from the command’s environment.
Changes to this directory before running the command.
Separates the printed variables with a null byte instead of a newline.

arguments.name: NAME=VALUE
arguments.description: Variables to set for the command.

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: Program to run with this environment.

examples.explanation: Runs ls with messages and dates in plain English (C locale), without changing the shell.
Opens a shell with an empty environment, to test a script without your personal settings.
